question: Which of the following states comes under the area of low rainfall?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gujarat is one of the states in India that experiences low rainfall.**
 
• Other states **that experience low rainfall include Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, and Punjab.** 
 
• Areas that receive 50 centimeters or less of rainfall are considered low rainfall regions. 
 
• The** Kutch region of Gujarat and western Rajasthan receive less than average rainfall. **
 
• The Thar Desert and the Himalayas impact the distribution of rainfall in India. 
 
• The moisture-bearing winds of the southwest monsoon gradually decrease in moisture as they move inland, resulting in low rainfall in western India. 
 
• The **economy of Bihar is threatened by declining rainfall, which affects its rain-fed agriculture. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India mainly receives rainfall from the Monsoons which lasts from June-September. Overall, India receives an average of 200-300 mm of rainfall over the country as a whole with the largest values observed during the monsoon season.
 
• The average annual rainfall in India is about 300–650 millimeters.
 
• The rainy season in India is affected by the humid southwest summer monsoon.
 
• The South of India typically receives more rainfall
 
• According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Mahabaleshwar has recorded the highest rainfall even more than Mawsynram, in Meghalaya. Now, it is considered the wettest place in India.
 
• Jaisalmer is considered the driest place in India to have received the minimum or scanty rainfall over the years.
